data: private real-label M60 conditional panels, three tasks, three edit densities
protocol: train on two tasks, question-disjoint test on the held-out task, three seeds
conclusion: The learned selector has a task-dependent signal. It improves the held-out CommonsenseQA transfer cell but loses on SciQ and ties on QASC. No robust service-quality winner is established.
limitations: The panels use the existing M60 conditional interface and do not constitute a new sealed benchmark.
No claim of ACL Main readiness is made.
